## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, … [truncated]

{"baseRefName":"main","body":"**Draft: this PR is intentionally red.** It adds one failing test and no fix, to pin a pre-existing bug ahead of fixing it. Do not merge as-is.

Surfaced while reviewing #116. That PR fixes the *one-shot* instance of this mistake (`653e9c5`); this is the batched instance, which predates both and is disclosed in #116's known-limitations, tracked in [ENT-2060](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-2060/bootstrap-resume-partial-progress-subset-resume-and-a-sync-mode-route).

## The bug

A batched bootstrap's temp ref `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/<branch>` is the only record of how far an import got. The cutover push carries two commands in one request — advance the temp ref to the final checkpoint, and create the real branch there — and `bootstrap.go:654` deletes the temp ref immediately afterwards on the strength of that push returning no error.

Under `--best-effort` that inference is invalid. `gitproto/push.go:453-470` hands a per-ref `ng` to `OnRejection` and returns `nil`, so a target that refuses the branch create (protected branch, pre-receive policy) ends the run with **neither the branch nor the marker**, reporting success:

```
[server] request with 2 command(s), rejecting only refs/heads/master:
  refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/master c416d48f -> cbfbb940 : ok
  refs/heads/master                   <zero>   -> cbfbb940 : ng rejected by policy

Run() error : <nil>          ← exit 0
Pushed/Warned/BatchCount : 0 / 1 / 8
target after run: branch present=false, marker present=false
```

The guard at `:647` can't catch it either — it consults `p.TargetRefs`, the ref map captured at session start, not re-read after the push.

## Why it matters

The rejection itself is surfaced honestly (`Pushed: 0`, `Warned: 1`, plan `action=warn`). What is surfaced nowhere is that the run also destroyed the checkpoint, and the process exits 0.

With the marker gone and the branch never created, every object pushed so far is unreferenced on the target: nothing points at it, so the next run has no fetch have to negotiate against and re-transfers the entire history — and the target is free to GC it meanwhile. Batching is by definition the large-repo path (ENT-1948, >10 GiB), so this costs exactly the imports that can least afford it.

It needs the rejection reaching the strategy. The syncer already records it (`s.rejections`, `syncer.go:708`), so it's a `Params` field plus a check at the cutover:

```go
Rejected func(plumbing.ReferenceName) bool
```

skip the temp-ref delete when the branch create was refused, and the next run resumes from the marker instead of starting over.

I prototyped exactly that locally: the new test passes and the **full suite stays green**. The prototype was then reverted, so this branch is test-only — but the test pins the real defect rather than being red for an incidental reason.

## Note on the test

It applies the non-denied commands itself rather than using `syncertest.DenyRefsReport`. A non-nil report short-circuits the test server *before* it applies anything, which would leave the temp ref at the previous checkpoint and make the delete that follows carry a stale `Old` — a shape a real receive-pack would reject, hiding the bug behind a second failure. Applying the advance keeps the sequence faithful: the marker genuinely reaches the final checkpoint, and is then genuinely destroyed. {"body":"Fixes [ENT-2054](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-2054/interrupted-batched-bootstrap-can-never-resume-the-resume-ref) — an interrupted batched bootstrap could never resume, because its own resume marker disqualified the bootstrap route. [ENT-1948](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1948/mirror-sync-permanently-fails-when-catch-up-pack-exceeds-10-gib) is one instance.

## The bug

Batched bootstrap writes `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/<branch>` so an interrupted run can resume. Under `replicate --all-refs --prune` (the mirror-worker shape), that marker was just an undesired target ref of `RefKindOther`, so `replicateCanBootstrap` returned false and every subsequent sync routed to `replicate` — a single unbatched pack. The artifact of the one strategy that can resume is exactly what locked that strategy out, permanently.

## The fix

`replicateBootstrapRoute` routes on the marker's presence, ahead of the emptiness heuristic. The namespace has exactly one writer — batched bootstrap, which deletes its marker on finalize or when stale — so a surviving marker for a branch **in the desired set** is a positive signal: a bootstrap started and did not finish. The route requires every desired target ref to be absent (the bootstrap planner refuses targets whose desired refs exist) and deliberately ignores other stray target refs, so an aborted push or a branch deleted upstream mid-bootstrap cannot re-wedge the repo. It is gated on the source supporting batched bootstrap (protocol v2 + fetch filter); a non-batchable source stands down rather than trade a marker-anchored delta for a one-shot full pack. The reason `bootstrap-resume-marker` is threaded through dry-run, so a plan against a stranded repo confirms the routing in one shot.

**Marker lifecycle.** Prune is the marker's cleaner, and the exception that protects a live one is stated once, at prune candidacy (`addPruneCandidates`), so every plan builder is covered — including `sync --prune`, which previously would have deleted a resume position. A marker is live exactly while its branch is desired and absent; once the branch lands it is stale and prunes normally. Notably the bootstrap strategy does **not** delete the marker on the one-shot path: a nil push error doesn't prove the create landed (BestEffort swallows a per-ref `ng`), so deferring to prune costs one run and cannot be wrong. The one-shot path also passes target refs as fetch haves, so a small-repo resume transfers only the remainder.

## Behavior changes beyond the routing fix

- **`refs/gitsync/*` is no longer mirrored from a source.** Under `--all-refs`, a source ref in that namespace is now skipped by discovery. Such a ref is leftover scaffolding from that repo having been someone else's sync target, and mirroring it would collide with — and under replicate's overwrite semantics, clobber — this target's own resume marker. Consequence worth knowing: a source holding **only** that scaffolding now yields an empty desired set and errors (`no source refs matched` / `ErrNoRefsSelected`) where it previously converged. Deliberate; it clears once that source's own bootstrap resumes, which this PR is what makes possible.
- Target-side prune scope is unchanged — stale markers must stay reapable.

## Deliberately not done

- **Deletes-before-updates in `replicate.Execute`** (floated in the ticket): the update-then-delete order is load-bearing for mirror-worker's default-branch rename recovery (`cmd/worker/defaultbranch.go:67`), which relies on the replacement branch existing before entiredb rejects the current-branch delete. With routing fixed, marker cleanup no longer gates anything.
- **The `excludeRefPrefixes` stopgap in mirror-worker**: hiding `refs/gitsync/` from the sync scope would block stale-marker pruning forever, and saves no deploy.

## Known limitations — tracked in [ENT-2060](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-2060/bootstrap-resume-partial-progress-subset-resume-and-a-sync-mode-route)

- **Partial progress doesn't resume**: a multi-branch bootstrap interrupted after one branch finalized has a non-absent desired ref, so the remainder still goes as one replicate pack (marker-anchored, but unsubdividable).
- **Sync mode has no resume route** — only its destructive half is fixed here.
- Stale markers under `--map` or branch-scoped prune have no cleaner; the batched cutover deletes its temp ref on a best-effort create too (pre-existing, same hazard class as the one fixed here); dry-run doesn't disclose marker lifecycle.

## Rollout

`vc3r` / `rci` heal once mirror-pipeline's git-sync pin is bumped past this and deployed. The companion worker change — logging `operation_mode` / `transfer_mode` / `relay_reason`, whose absence is why ENT-2054 took a code read instead of a log query — is independent and on the same-named mirror-pipeline branch.

## Tests

- Routing table: marker+absent → bootstrap; marker+present branch → replicate; marker+stray ref → bootstrap; orphan marker → replicate; non-batchable source → replicate; no-prune resume labeling; empty target → emptiness reason.
- `TestRun_IntegrationReplicateResumesInterruptedBatchedBootstrap`: interrupts a batched bootstrap mid-checkpoint under the exact mirror-worker shape, asserts dry-run reports `bootstrap-resume-marker`, and asserts the retry's first temp-ref push resumes **from the marker hash** — not from zero.
- `TestRun_IntegrationResumeMarkerSurvivesBestEffortRejectedCreate`: a best-effort run whose branch create is rejected must leave the marker intact. Fails without the cleanup removal.
- `TestRun_IntegrationReplicateOrphanMarkerPrunedInOneRun`: pre-PR one-run parity for a marker whose branch was deleted upstream.
- Plus planner tests for the discovery exclusion and the prune guard (both builders), the non-batchable fallback, and one-shot resume (mid-chain and at-tip markers).

Full suite and golangci-lint green.

{"id":"ENT-2054","title":"Interrupted batched bootstrap can never resume: the resume ref disqualifies the bootstrap route","description":"## Summary

git-sync's batched bootstrap writes a resume marker (`refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/<branch>`) so an interrupted run can pick up where it left off. It also has real logic to do that: `BootstrapResumeIndex`, chain-position recovery, and the "resuming from stale temp ref" re-plan at `bootstrap.go:352`.

**That logic is unreachable from mirror-worker.** The marker it resumes from is exactly what stops the bootstrap strategy from being selected on the next pass. Once a batched bootstrap is interrupted for any reason, the repo is routed to `replicate` forever — and `replicate` has no batching.

<issue id="5b7a6b15-b273-4116-a4a4-0c2147883e72" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1948/mirror-sync-permanently-fails-when-catch-up-pack-exceeds-10-gib">ENT-1948</issue> is one instance of this (the interruption there was the 10 GiB receive-pack cap). This ticket is the reason that instance never heals, and it generalises past that cap.

## The chain

All read in code, not inferred:

1. mirror-worker syncs with `AllRefs: true` + `Prune: true` and no `Mappings` — `mirror-pipeline/cmd/worker/syncer.go:652` (`refScopeFor`), `:707` (`syncPolicyFor`).
2. `excludeRefPrefixes` (`cmd/worker/syncer.go:80-105`) does **not** contain `refs/gitsync/`. It carves out other tooling-owned namespaces — `refs/tlog/`, `refs/meta/entire/`, `refs/internal/` — but this one was missed.
3. `syncer.replicateCanBootstrap` (`git-sync/internal/syncer/syncer.go:1157`) passes its desired-refs loop (the target genuinely has no `refs/heads/main`), but because `Prune` is set it then walks **every** target ref. `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/main` is non-zero, not desired, and not excluded; `planner.RefKindFromName` returns `RefKindOther` (`planner/types.go:142` — `IsBranch()` requires a `refs/heads/` prefix), which matches the `AllRefs && RefKindOther && no Mappings` case → **returns false**.
4. `allAbsent == false` → `bootstrapWithInputs` is skipped → `BuildReplicationPlans` → `executeReplicate` → a single unbatched pack.
5. When that push fails, the temp ref is never cleaned up either: `replicate.Execute` pushes updates before deletes and returns on update failure (`internal/strategy/replicate/replicate.go:62-79`), so the prune that would have removed the marker never runs.

Every subsequent sync makes the identical decision. The artifact of the one attempt that *was* using the right strategy is what locks that strategy out.

## Scope

Any repo whose batched bootstrap is interrupted — OOM, pod eviction, deploy, context cancel, deadline, or a receive-pack rejection. The interruption cause is incidental; the lock is the same. Confirmed instance: `gh/nicschick/vc3r` (`01KXK4WZWXD1PEP16K9V6CMFHA`, eu-central-1), stranded since 2026-07-15, ~5 MB / 19 loose objects / 0 packfiles behind a bootstrap temp ref with no `refs/heads/main`.

`refs/gitsync/` is written **only** by git-sync — constructed in one place, `planner.BootstrapTempRef` (`internal/planner/types.go:227`) — and git-sync deletes it itself on success (`bootstrap.go:654`) or when stale (`:378`). entiredb has no awareness of the namespace at all (no references in `refpolicy`, `server`, or `mirror`), so it is an ordinary ref there: listable, pushable, prunable. A leftover `refs/gitsync/*` ref therefore means one thing only — a bootstrap that did not finish — and nothing outside git-sync reads it.

### Second instance: `gh/nicschick/rci`

`01KXK4WZS7M270NSABM94DRF01`, same GitHub App install (146778232), created within the same minute as `vc3r` on 2026-07-15. Identical ref shape — `HEAD` → `refs/heads/main` (absent) plus `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/main` → `93b964ac`, nothing else.

It matters because **its interruption was demonstrably not the 10 GiB cap**: 4 packfiles totalling 354 MB were written between 15:09:36Z and 15:50:59Z on 2026-07-15, so the fetch landed, and it has **zero **`@target_ulid` telemetry in the last 30 days — no sync jobs at all, failing or otherwise. Most likely a dormant upstream (no pushes → no jobs). That makes it a *latent* instance rather than an actively-burning one: the moment a push arrives it takes exactly the path described above.

This is the concrete evidence for the "interruption cause is incidental" claim in Scope — two repos, same lock, different interruptions.

## Proposed fixes

**Primary — see the marker and resume from it.** Route on the marker's *presence*: a `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/*` ref means a bootstrap started and did not finish, which is strictly more information than "the target has no managed refs". Check it ahead of the emptiness heuristic and send the repo to the bootstrap strategy, which then resumes from that exact ref.

Why this shape rather than hiding the ref:

* **It is a positive signal.** The namespace has exactly one writer and exactly one meaning. Using it directly is honest; the alternative below makes the system conclude "this repo is empty", which is false — it is half-bootstrapped. Right routing for the wrong reason.
* **It does not depend on the marker being the only stray ref.** The exclusion works on `vc3r` only because nothing else sits in the target ref map. One additional leftover ref — an aborted sync, a branch deleted upstream mid-bootstrap, a manual push — and the repo wedges again for the same underlying reason.
* The resume machinery is already written and currently unreachable. `BootstrapResumeIndex`, the chain-position re-plan (`bootstrap.go:352`), stale-marker deletion (`:378`), and the per-branch subsume when a branch is already complete (`:249`). This is the wiring that turns all of it on rather than new logic.

Edge cases the existing code already covers: a stale marker (pointing at a commit no longer in the source chain) is re-planned from its chain position or deleted; a marker left behind on an otherwise-complete repo degrades to a no-op via the per-branch subsume check.

**Stopgap (one line, unblocks today):** add `refs/gitsync/` to `excludeRefPrefixes` in `cmd/worker/syncer.go:80`, alongside the existing `refs/tlog/` and `refs/meta/entire/` entries. This makes the marker invisible to `replicateCanBootstrap`, so the check returns "bootstrappable" and the repo takes the bootstrap path. Useful to unblock `vc3r` now, but it is not the end state — see the second bullet above for why it is fragile.

**Also worth doing:** run deletes before updates in `replicate.Execute` (`internal/strategy/replicate/replicate.go:62-79`), so a prune still lands when the pack push fails. Independent of the above, and closes the "the failure prevents its own cleanup" half of the trap.

**Considered and set aside:** routing on entiredb's `MirrorInitialSyncDone` flag. It tells you the import is unfinished but not *where to pick up*, and it needs plumbing from entiredb into the job payload. The marker answers both questions and is already local to git-sync.

## Implementation notes

For whoever picks this up — routing to bootstrap is necessary but not automatically sufficient:

* **Auto-batching is gated on source capability. **`SupportsBootstrapBatch()` (`internal/gitproto/fetch.go:33`) requires `Protocol == "v2"` **and **`V2Caps.FetchSupports("filter")`. True for GitHub, so `vc3r` is fine — but a non-v2 source would reach bootstrap and still fail unbatched. Any fix that only changes routing inherits this gate.
* **Setting** `TargetMaxPackBytes` **in the worker would *disable* the reactive path. **`autoTargetMaxPackBytes` returns early when `p.TargetMaxPack > 0` (`bootstrap.go:1386`). mirror-worker currently passes no pack options at all (`cmd/worker/syncer.go:399`), which is precisely why auto-detection is eligible. Counterintuitive — worth a comment at whichever site ends up owning it.
* **Batch sizing:** the auto path takes the min of `defaultTargetMaxPackBytes` (512 MiB), half the limit announced in the rejection, and `MaxPackBytes` when set.
* **Subdivision has a floor. **`subdivideCheckpoints` halves commit ranges until every gap is one commit, so a *single* commit whose delta exceeds the cap still fails. Not yet checked whether `vc3r`'s >10 GiB spans multiple commits — worth confirming before assuming this fix converges that specific repo.
* **The target must permit non-fast-forward updates on** `refs/gitsync/` (`git-sync/docs/usage.md:97`, `unstable/client.go:52`). Fine today since entiredb has no policy on the namespace, but it constrains any future reserved-ref work there.

## Verification status

The chain above is read from source and matches the error string observed in <issue id="5b7a6b15-b273-4116-a4a4-0c2147883e72" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1948/mirror-sync-permanently-fails-when-catch-up-pack-exceeds-10-gib">ENT-1948</issue> (`replicate relay failed: replicate execute: push target refs: ...`). The routing decision itself is **not** logged — mirror-worker records `operation: sync_repo` but not the sync result's `OperationMode` / `RelayReason`. A `git-sync` dry-run against that source/target prints `BootstrapSuggested` and `RelayReason` directly and would confirm it in one shot.

**Suggested follow-up regardless of fix:** log `OperationMode` and `RelayReason` from mirror-worker. git-sync's batched bootstrap writes a resume marker (`refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/<branch>`) so an interrupted run can pick up where it left off. It also has real logic to do that: `BootstrapResumeIndex`, chain-position recovery, and the "resuming from stale temp ref" re-plan at `bootstrap.go:352`.

**That logic is unreachable from mirror-worker.** The marker it resumes from is exactly what stops the bootstrap strategy from being selected on the next pass. Once a batched bootstrap is interrupted for any reason, the repo is routed to `replicate` forever — and `replicate` has no batching.

<issue id="5b7a6b15-b273-4116-a4a4-0c2147883e72" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1948/mirror-sync-permanently-fails-when-catch-up-pack-exceeds-10-gib">ENT-1948</issue> is one instance of this (the interruption there was the 10 GiB receive-pack cap). This ticket is the reason that instance never heals, and it generalises past that cap.

## The chain

All read in code, not inferred:

1. mirror-worker syncs with `AllRefs: true` + `Prune: true` and no `Mappings` — `mirror-pipeline/cmd/worker/syncer.go:652` (`refScopeFor`), `:707` (`syncPolicyFor`).
2. `excludeRefPrefixes` (`cmd/worker/syncer.go:80-105`) does **not** contain `refs/gitsync/`. It carves out other tooling-owned namespaces — `refs/tlog/`, `refs/meta/entire/`, `refs/internal/` — but this one was missed.
3. `syncer.replicateCanBootstrap` (`git-sync/internal/syncer/syncer.go:1157`) passes its desired-refs loop (the target genuinely has no `refs/heads/main`), but because `Prune` is set it then walks **every** target ref. `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/main` is non-zero, not desired, and not excluded; `planner.RefKindFromName` returns `RefKindOther` (`planner/types.go:142` — `IsBranch()` requires a `refs/heads/` prefix), which matches the `AllRefs && RefKindOther && no Mappings` case → **returns false**.
4. `allAbsent == false` → `bootstrapWithInputs` is skipped → `BuildReplicationPlans` → `executeReplicate` → a single unbatched pack.
5. When that push fails, the temp ref is never cleaned up either: `replicate.Execute` pushes updates before deletes and returns on update failure (`internal/strategy/replicate/replicate.go:62-79`), so the prune that would have removed the marker never runs.

Every subsequent sync makes the identical decision. The artifact of the one attempt that *was* using the right strategy is what locks that strategy out.

## Scope

Any repo whose batched bootstrap is interrupted — OOM, pod eviction, deploy, context cancel, deadline, or a receive-pack rejection. The interruption cause is incidental; the lock is the same. Confirmed instance: `gh/nicschick/vc3r` (`01KXK4WZWXD1PEP16K9V6CMFHA`, eu-central-1), stranded since 2026-07-15, ~5 MB / 19 loose objects / 0 packfiles behind a bootstrap temp ref with no `refs/heads/main`.

`refs/gitsync/` is written **only** by git-sync — constructed in one place, `planner.BootstrapTempRef` (`internal/planner/types.go:227`) — and git-sync deletes it itself on success (`bootstrap.go:654`) or when stale (`:378`). entiredb has no awareness of the namespace at all (no references in `refpolicy`, `server`, or `mirror`), so it is an ordinary ref there: listable, pushable, prunable. A leftover `refs/gitsync/*` ref therefore means one thing only — a bootstrap that did not finish — and nothing outside git-sync reads it.

### Second instance: `gh/nicschick/rci`

`01KXK4WZS7M270NSABM94DRF01`, same GitHub App install (146778232), created within the same minute as `vc3r` on 2026-07-15. Identical ref shape — `HEAD` → `refs/heads/main` (absent) plus `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/main` → `93b964ac`, nothing else.

It matters because **its interruption was demonstrably not the 10 GiB cap**: 4 packfiles totalling 354 MB were written between 15:09:36Z and 15:50:59Z on 2026-07-15, so the fetch landed, and it has **zero **`@target_ulid` telemetry in the last 30 days — no sync jobs at all, failing or otherwise. Most likely a dormant upstream (no pushes → no jobs). That makes it a *latent* instance rather than an actively-burning one: the moment a push arrives it takes exactly the path described above.

This is the concrete evidence for the "interruption cause is incidental" claim in Scope — two repos, same lock, different interruptions.

## Proposed fixes

**Primary — see the marker and resume from it.** Route on the marker's *presence*: a `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/*` ref means a bootstrap started and did not finish, which is strictly more information than "the target has no managed refs". Check it ahead of the emptiness heuristic and send the repo to the bootstrap strategy, which then resumes from that exact ref.

Why this shape rather than hiding the ref:

* **It is a positive signal.** The namespace has exactly one writer and exactly one meaning. Using it directly is honest; the alternative below makes the system conclude "this repo is empty", which is false — it is half-bootstrapped. Right routing for the wrong reason.
* **It does not depend on the marker being the only stray ref.** The exclusion works on `vc3r` only because nothing else sits in the target ref map. One additional leftover ref — an aborted sync, a branch deleted upstream mid-bootstrap, a manual push — and the repo wedges again for the same underlying reason.
* The resume machinery is already written and currently unreachable. `BootstrapResumeIndex`, the chain-position re-plan (`bootstrap.go:352`), stale-marker deletion (`:378`), and the per-branch subsume when a branch is already complete (`:249`). This is the wiring that turns all of it on rather than new logic.

Edge cases the existing code already covers: a stale marker (pointing at a commit no longer in the source chain) is re-planned from its chain position or deleted; a marker left behind on an otherwise-complete repo degrades to a no-op via the per-branch subsume check.

**Stopgap (one line, unblocks today):** add `refs/gitsync/` to `excludeRefPrefixes` in `cmd/worker/syncer.go:80`, alongside the existing `refs/tlog/` and `refs/meta/entire/` entries. This makes the marker invisible to `replicateCanBootstrap`, so the check returns "bootstrappable" and the repo takes the bootstrap path. Useful to unblock `vc3r` now, but it is not the end state — see the second bullet above for why it is fragile.

**Also worth doing:** run deletes before updates in `replicate.Execute` (`internal/strategy/replicate/replicate.go:62-79`), so a prune still lands when the pack push fails. Independent of the above, and closes the "the failure prevents its own cleanup" half of the trap.

**Considered and set aside:** routing on entiredb's `MirrorInitialSyncDone` flag. It tells you the import is unfinished but not *where to pick up*, and it needs plumbing from entiredb into the job payload. The marker answers both questions and is already local to git-sync.

## Implementation notes

For whoever picks this up — routing to bootstrap is necessary but not automatically sufficient:

* **Auto-batching is gated on source capability. **`SupportsBootstrapBatch()` (`internal/gitproto/fetch.go:33`) requires `Protocol == "v2"` **and **`V2Caps.FetchSupports("filter")`. * **Setting** `TargetMaxPackBytes` **in the worker would *disable* the reactive path. **`autoTargetMaxPackBytes` returns early when `p.TargetMaxPack > 0` (`bootstrap.go:1386`). mirror-worker currently passes no pack options at all (`cmd/worker/syncer.go:399`), which is precisely why auto-detection is eligible. Counterintuitive — worth a comment at whichever site ends up owning it.
* **Batch sizing:** the auto path takes the min of `defaultTargetMaxPackBytes` (512 MiB), half the limit announced in the rejection, and `MaxPackBytes` when set.
* **Subdivision has a floor. **`subdivideCheckpoints` halves commit ranges until every gap is one commit, so a *single* commit whose delta exceeds the cap still fails. Not yet checked whether `vc3r`'s >10 GiB spans multiple commits — worth confirming before assuming this fix converges that specific repo.

Author: Andrea Nodari <andrea@entire.io>

    Address review: stop deleting the resume marker on a create we can't confirm
    
    The one-shot path's temp-ref cleanup assumed a nil push error meant every ref
    it planned had landed. Under BestEffort that is false: the pusher swallows a
    per-ref "ng" and returns nil (gitproto.PushPack via OnRejection), so a run
    whose branch create was rejected still reported success — and then deleted
    the marker recording how far the interrupted bootstrap got. Reachable from
    the CLI, where --all-refs implies best-effort.
    
    Cleanup is dropped rather than made conditional. Prune already classifies the
    marker correctly (branch present -> stale -> pruned; absent -> live -> kept),
    so deferring to it costs one extra run and cannot be wrong, where any
    strategy-side check would be re-deriving what the planner already knows from
    a signal the strategy cannot see.
    
    The one-shot integration test now asserts the marker survives the resuming
    run and is pruned by the run after, and a new test pins the hazard directly:
    a best-effort run whose branch create is rejected must leave the marker at
    its original hash. It fails without this change. Note for whoever writes the
    next one of these: a non-nil receivePackHook report short-circuits the test

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [0.9.0] - 2026-08-28

### Security

- Bumped `golang.org/x/crypto` to `v0.54.0`, closing 13 Dependabot alerts (7 critical, 3 high, 3 medium), all of them in its SSH implementation. Raised as an indirect dependency via minimal version selection, since go-git still asks for `v0.51.0`; lifts `golang.org/x/net` to `v0.56.0` and `golang.org/x/sys` to `v0.47.0` ([#104](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/104))

- Bumped go-git to `v6.0.0-alpha.5`, clearing two advisories `govulncheck` reported as reachable from git-sync's own call graph: **GO-2026-6214**, path traversal via crafted reference names, reached where `convert-sha256` writes advertised refs to disk; and **GO-2026-6213**, worktree operations following symlinks. Pulls `go-billy` to `v6.0.0-alpha.2` transitively ([#105](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/105), [#106](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/106))

- Bumped the Go toolchain to `1.26.6` (go.mod `toolchain` and the mise pin), clearing ten standard-library advisories reachable from the HTTP transport and the `convert-sha256` filesystem paths — among them quadratic complexity in `net/url` `resolvePath`, an `os` root escape via symlink plus trailing slash, and an HTTP/2 infinite loop on a bad `SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE`. Released binaries are built from the go.mod toolchain, so they carried these until now; `govulncheck ./...` goes from 12 called vulnerabilities to 0 ([#106](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/106))

- **Explicitly supplied credentials are now bound to the host you named.** Under `--source-follow-info-refs-redirect` / `--target-follow-info-refs-redirect`, git-sync addresses the host `/info/refs` redirected to directly for the follow-up RPCs, and re-attached the configured REDACTED to those requests after Go's `http.Client` had deliberately stripped the `Authorization` header on the cross-host hop — so any redirect an attacker could cause (an open redirect on the real host, a hostile mirror, a man-in-the-middle on a plain-`http` source) collected a REDACTED that on the target side typically carries write access. A REDACTED now goes only to the host named on the command line and its subdomains, on the same port and without a scheme downgrade, and anything else falls through to the credential helper with a warning naming the withheld host. Credentials resolved *from* the helper are unaffected — those were always looked up keyed on the host being challenged ([#108](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/108))

- **Ref names from a remote are validated before git-sync acts on them.** Unchecked names reached two places where a malformed one matters: `convert-sha256` writes them to disk, where `refs/heads/../../config` escapes `refs/heads` (go-billy clamps the traversal at the repository root, so the reachable damage is overwriting `config`, `HEAD`, or `packed-refs`); and ref-update commands embed them in the receive-pack request, where a NUL lets the source inject a capability list into the push git-sync sends to the *target*. Advertised names now go through `plumbing.ReferenceName.Validate` — git's own `check_refname_format`, so nothing git accepts is affected — at both decode boundaries, on the source and target side. A failing name is skipped with a quoted warning rather than failing the run; names supplied through `--map` are rejected outright at startup ([#109](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/109))

- **A packfile object header can no longer request an unbounded allocation.** `ExtractCommitParents` sized its per-object buffer from the size the pack header *declares*, which go-git validates only for varint overflow — so the value is remote-controlled up to `int64`, and a 48-byte pack declaring a 128 TiB object produced `fatal error: out of memory`, a Go runtime fatal an embedding process cannot contain with `recover()`. Declared sizes above 64 MiB are now rejected (this path reads `tree:0`-filtered packs, whose objects are commits and tags measured in kilobytes) and the initial buffer is capped at 64 KiB, so the allocation tracks bytes actually received. Reachable from ordinary planning, via `FetchCommitParents` during ancestry checks ([#107](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/107))

- **SSH repository paths are now shell-quoted in full.** `shellQuotePath` exempted the segment before the first slash when the path began with `~`, leaving it for the remote login shell to expand — and a SCP-style URL puts attacker-influenceable text in exactly that position: `git@host:~a;id/repo.git` produced the remote command `git-upload-pack ~a;id/'repo.git'`, executing `id` on the remote host as the authenticated SSH user. This matters wherever only part of the URL is caller-controlled, such as a repository path templated into a fixed host or one arriving from a webhook. Quoting the whole path costs nothing, because `git-upload-pack` resolves it through `enter_repo()`, which interpolates a leading `~` itself ([#107](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/107))

- **Credentials embedded in a remote URL are no longer echoed.** `probe` and `fetch` carried `Source.URL`/`Target.URL` verbatim into their results, which are printed to stdout and serialized into `--json` — so `REDACTED`, the standard CI form, put the REDACTED in output that automation collects; the URL-parse failure path leaked it too, since `url.Parse` embeds the raw URL in its error. All of these now redact the whole userinfo component via the new `internal/redact` package, which also replaces `url.URL.Redacted()` in HTTP error messages: `Redacted()` masks only the password, leaving a REDACTED in the *username* position — how GitHub App and PAT URLs are normally written — in the clear ([#107](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/107))

- **The materialized object limit is enforced while the pack streams, not after.** `FetchToStore` filled the in-memory store with no cap, and `--materialized-max-objects` (default 500,000) was checked against the object closure only once the fetch had finished — by which point the objects were resident and the process may already have died, so the guard reported an overrun it exists to prevent. The store now enforces the count as objects are decoded, failing the write that would exceed the limit, with an `ErrObjectLimit` sentinel and an `ObjectLimitError` carrying the limit. git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Keep the batched resume marker when the target refuses the branch create

The batched cutover deleted its temp ref on the strength of a nil push error,
and under BestEffort that error covers the request rather than each command in
it: the pusher hands a per-ref "ng" to OnRejection and returns nil. So a target
that refused the branch create — protected branch, pre-receive policy — ended
the run with neither the branch nor the marker, reported as a success. With
nothing on the target pointing at the objects already pushed, the next run had
no have to negotiate against and re-transferred the whole history, on precisely
the large repositories batching exists for (ENT-1948, >10 GiB). Reachable
wherever best-effort is implied: --all-refs turns it on for bootstrap and sync,
and client.go passes Policy.BestEffort through for any mode.

The rejection now reaches the strategy. Params.Rejected is a predicate the
syncer answers from the map it already fills from the pusher's OnRejection
callback, and the cutover consults it before deleting: a create this run cannot
confirm leaves the marker at the final checkpoint, so the next run resumes from
it. The delete is made conditional rather than dropped the way PR #116 dropped
the one-shot path's: Bootstrap() rejects --prune outright, so on that route no
cleaner would ever exist and the marker would be permanent.

The kept marker is also recorded as a completed ref, since it genuinely holds
that hash — the objects behind it stay usable as haves for the branches planned
after this one. The rejection itself was already surfaced honestly (Pushed 0,
Warned 1, plan action=warn); what was surfaced nowhere is that the run also
destroyed the checkpoint, so retaining it now logs and prints a line naming the
marker and the hash it resumes from.

Tests: the pinned test from this branch now passes, and a companion asserts the
half that makes the marker worth keeping — the retry, once the target accepts
the create, finishes the import from the marker (zero checkpoint packs, 334
bytes to the target against the first run's 427 KiB) and only then deletes it.

carrying the reason it cannot use syncertest.DenyRefsReport.
